pairs.subject: review-iteration-loops
pairs.evidence: apps/console/src/pages/review/Layer1.tsx:54 The page reviews sandbox sessions only after they have ended and has no path that revises, edits or regenerates the reviewed transcript (a search of apps/console/src/pages/review, tests included, for regenerat/revision/editPlan/edit_plan/attribution found nothing); operator marks go to review.feedback.set and the daemon's tone inbox, where they become bank candidates and direction suggestions for future runs, so the subject's precondition — answering notes on reviewed work with a revision — does not hold here.

techniques.evidence: apps/console/src/pages/review/Layer1.tsx:54 Sessions are reviewed after they end and are never revised, so there is no revision path that could edit or regenerate.

apps/console/src/pages/review/FeedbackPanel.tsx:57 The closed mark set (landed/flat/too_mean/off_tone/...) labels the quality of an aired line for tone learning. Marks are not focus/scope/order requests against a revisable piece, so there are no minimal edit operations to map them to.

apps/console/src/pages/review/Judge.tsx:58 Judge findings are rendered for a human operator who decides, not for an automated stage that acts. The technique's own boundary says not to demote such findings by fixability.

pairs.registryProposal: The registry map matched this subject to the context with 'strong' confidence on the tokens review/feedback/panel. But the subject presumes the reviewed artifact will be revised. A post-hoc review surface whose marks only train future generations (eval labels feeding a tone or bank inbox) is a different loop, and nothing in this subject governs it. Consider a use_when exclusion, or a technique for 'review labels that feed learning rather than revision'.
